correctness.rationale: The original residual-diagonal sampler reduces exactly to successive sampling without replacement on diagonal weights. Exact product and determinant subset counting give both spike-omission probabilities. Symmetry determines the other m omission marginals, while diagonal RKHS duality supplies the exact optimal-weight squared error. Strict P_R<P_D follows by a derivative comparison from equality at L=1; high-L asymptotics follow from finite products. Every formula is checked against complete rational enumeration on finite parameter ranges. Tests corroborate but do not prove the universal claims.

originality.rationale: At the level of the joint sharp target-risk theorem, available primary full-text statements and research search results did not identify prior coverage. Yu (2010) already establishes the relevant qualitative inclusion majorization, Belhadji et al. (2020) a determinant-sampling risk expansion, and Epperly–Moreno (2023) the RPChol quadrature method; these are credited rather than presented as new. The claimed contribution is the exact sign-indefinite all-target comparison and sharp unbounded expected-squared-error ratio on one finite kernel family. Earlier classical survey-sampling equivalences remain a residual risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent specialization might exist in classical successive-versus-rejective survey-sampling theory or finite diagonal Nyström literature under another name.
The qualitative spike-inclusion ordering is already implied by Yu (2010), so no novelty is claimed for that isolated inequality.
The example is an idealized discrete one-spike kernel and does not establish a generic continuous-domain sampling comparison.

value.rationale: The 2023 RPChol quadrature paper specifically invites sharper comparisons or separations from volume sampling. The theorem answers a concrete, motivated part: for every target density on a natural finite spectral test kernel it identifies which sampler wins, including a nontrivial sign-indefinite difference and a sharp unbounded ratio where volume sampling retains a positive expected squared-error floor. This is a reproducible benchmark on which generic trace-error bounds do not capture target sensitivity. The result is narrow but complete, and makes no unsupported generic kernel superiority claim.
